rubrics.criterion: After the patch, the complete supported-language roster that the publishing pipeline consumes is declared in the repository's shared locale module (scripts/locales.ts), and every publishing stage that needs to know which languages exist obtains that set from there (by import or call) rather than from a stage-local re-declaration.
rubrics.rationale: This is the instance's central semantic outcome: the case scatters the 'which languages exist' knowledge across eight publishing sites, so the repair is only real if the shared locale module is once again the sole declarer of the complete set and the stages actually consult it.

rubrics.criterion: The rule for how localized artifact names are formed (the default language keeps the bare file name, every other language carries its own code as an infix) is likewise owned by the shared locale module, and every producer of localized names in the pipeline — the published artifact URL builders in scripts/toUrl.ts, README file naming in scripts/readme.ts, the machine-translation destination in scripts/translate.ts, and generic path resolution in scripts/utils/resolve.ts — derives its names through that shared source instead of stage-local infix tables or local case dispatch.
rubrics.rationale: The scattered knowledge in this case is not only the roster but the naming decision it drives; consolidating the list while leaving per-stage naming tables would keep the shotgun surgery in place for exactly the artifacts the pipeline publishes.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not merely move the complete language set or a complete infix table into a new non-owner module (a fresh file somewhere under scripts/ other than scripts/locales.ts that re-declares the full roster or full naming map), i.e. the consolidated knowledge lands in the existing shared locale module rather than a parallel one.
rubrics.rationale: A plausible failure mode for this instance: 'consolidating' by creating another shared-looking module outside scripts/locales.ts, which keeps a second owner of the roster and still forces every stage to track a module other than the locale module the repository already designates.

rubrics.criterion: Every stage that had grown a private language copy is rewired through the shared source: the site build's redirect generation and per-quiz emission loops (scripts/build.ts), README index and per-challenge regeneration plus the available-language link list (scripts/readme.ts), per-language sibling-file loading (scripts/loader.ts), the playground language argument and selection menu (scripts/generate-play.ts), the render-eligibility content choice (scripts/actions/utils/formatToCode.ts), the translation destination naming (scripts/translate.ts), and generic localized path resolution (scripts/utils/resolve.ts) — none of them still reads a stage-local roster copy or stage-local infix data.
rubrics.rationale: Shotgun surgery is only resolved when every consumer of the scattered knowledge actually participates in the new ownership; this instance's eight sites each consumed the knowledge differently (iteration, keys iteration, lookup, membership gate, menu choice, switch dispatch), so the grading must confirm all consumption styles were rewired.

rubrics.criterion: The shared locale module's exports were adjusted where needed so stages can genuinely defer everything they previously rebuilt: the shared module exposes the roster and the localized-naming decision in forms the stages can use directly for iteration, membership testing, selection, and name construction (for example a stage must not be forced to reconstruct infix knowledge from the roster on its own).
rubrics.rationale: Distinguishes a complete consolidation from one where the shared module was technically made the owner but does not actually provide the decision stages need, silently forcing per-stage reconstruction with slightly different code.

rubrics.criterion: The stage-local scaffolding injected alongside the copies is removed rather than abandoned: no orphaned local language table, list, switch dispatch, or naming helper remains anywhere under scripts/, and module import lists no longer contain imports that the rewired code no longer uses (e.g. an import of a removed table or of the old per-stage path helper that translate.ts used).
rubrics.rationale: Leaving dead local registries behind after rewiring is the natural residue of this reorganization and would keep the smell's debris in the codebase even after the ownership is restored.

rubrics.criterion: If the restructuring leaves a helper or module under scripts/ with no remaining callers (for example a path-resolution helper whose only consumer no longer needs it), it is removed instead of being kept as dead code; conversely, helpers that other modules still call are kept intact for those callers.
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific sanity that the cleanup went far enough to drop now-unused private helpers, while judging over-deletion by checking that helpers with remaining callers survive.

rubrics.criterion: The localized artifact naming scheme is unchanged in every artifact the pipeline produces: the default language still yields bare names (README.md, not README.en.md) and every other supported language still yields its code as an infix (README.zh-CN.md, README.ja.ts, and so on); no new or renamed file-name pattern (locale folders, hyphenation, uppercase codes, dropping the infix) appears anywhere in the pipeline.
rubrics.rationale: A naming consolidation that quietly changes even one published file name breaks every external link and the on-disk corpus layout, which is the highest-value behavior this instance must preserve.

rubrics.criterion: No supported language is dropped from or added to any stage's output as a side effect of the restructuring: redirects, emitted per-language files, README regeneration and the available-language links, variation file loading, the playground menu choices, and translation targets still cover exactly the same five supported languages as before the patch.
rubrics.rationale: A tempting shortcut for 'one place decides the languages' is to hard-code the default language or shrink the roster per stage; this instance's pipeline is multi-language by design, so every stage must keep processing the complete published set.

rubrics.criterion: Where the pre-patch code interpolated an infix for a language code outside the roster (generic path resolution and the localized-name builders when handed a not-yet-supported code), the patched code still interpolates that code in the same positions instead of throwing, returning an un-suffixed name, or silently mapping unknown codes to the default language's name.
rubrics.rationale: The escape-hatch behavior for not-yet-supported languages is easy to lose when replacing local tables with shared lookups, and losing it would send future translations, renders, and links to wrong paths.

rubrics.criterion: The restructuring leaves no dangling references: removed helpers, tables, or exports have no leftover call sites or imports anywhere in scripts/, and modules that legitimately continue to use the shared locale module's single-language facilities (defaultLocale, the translation lookup t(), the SupportedLocale type) still import them in a way that compiles and runs.
rubrics.rationale: Moving knowledge between modules in this pipeline necessarily churns import lists and call sites; incomplete rewiring that leaves broken or stale references is this instance's most likely collateral damage beyond the type-level test suite.

rubrics.criterion: Content selection still prefers the requested language's content and falls back to the default language's content only when the requested language has none — in particular the playground rendering gate must not start rejecting or mis-falling-back for a supported language that does have content, nor start emitting a supported language's content where the pipeline previously fell back.
rubrics.rationale: The render-eligibility gate was one of the scattered copies in this instance; reworking it to consult the shared roster is precisely where an over-eager gate could change which text ends up in generated playground files.
